Hello to all /v/manga users,

We are sorry for yet another rule change, we are still building this subverse and we appreciate any and all constructive feedback.

The rule we will be changing is:

Licensed -Licensed manga must either not be linked at all or it should be linked to an official source. You can check if manga has been licensed on MangaUpdates. Including links to buy the material is highly encouraged.

to

Manga chapters/volumes that have been licensed and published must either not be linked at all or it should be linked to an official source. You can check if manga has been licensed on MangaUpdates. Including links to buy the material is highly encouraged.

Examples:

Scenario 1: Katekyo Hitman Reborn was not licensed and printed beyond 16 volumes, therefore scans etc. of anything beyond volume 16 is fine.

Scenario 2: Shokugeki no Soma is currently licensed and printing, we do not know if/when it will stop, so we will not allow links to it.

Scenario 3: Prison School is licensed and not currently publishing, we will allow links until publishing begins and notify posters of discussions to remove links if we receive takedown requests.

Additionally, we'd like to draw attention to the reasoning of only allowing self posts when discussing manga.

Only discussion (self posts) are allowed for chapter/volume discussions of manga. If the manga is ever licensed, we'd like for you to be able to change the links instead of having to delete the post.

Reasoning behind both rules: We would like to avoid takedown requests as much as possible and hope proactively catching links but also avoid losing conversations between subverse members in the case such a request is sent to us. We felt having a restriction only on published/publishing manga would be a good compromise. Our highest reason in mind when deciding on using self (discussion) posts and not link posts was the fact that conversation would be preserved and accessible through the subverse search even in the event of a takedown request; the information only needs to be altered in the body instead of of needing a title edit, which is simply not allowed to begin with.

Another thing we'd like to note, as there seems to have been miscommunications...

We are not forcing people to not post and we never said people couldn't post their own discussions when we offered opening up 'official discussion threads from the mods'. The original intent was to offer an option to users who like the series' but don't want to post discussions themselves.

Thank you for your understanding, please feel free to post any constructive feedback here or in /v/MetaManga.

Good job! I was going to post on this as well. But there are three drug approaches that I know of:

Treventis has a Lead based compound TRV 101, Neurophage Pharm. has a phage protein based drug and then there is a monoclonal antibody drug out there. I'm betting on the Lead based compound. And all three of these drugs seem to have a wider applicability to not just AD but to Parkinson's and ALS and Lewy Body Dementia as well as other diseases as the misfolding mechanism is similar to all of these prion diseases.

Stage 1 trials are planned for TRV 101 and we should pressure the FDA to push this one forward once a dose has been found that is safe. Hell, what could be worse than AD? Death? No way.

BTW: This advance will be a massive blow to the long term prospects of the home health field and nursing home field. Think about it.

Well, these drugs probably won't be any worse than Namenda, Exelon, or Galantamine. They probably won't be any better either.

If there's a randomized, double-blind trial on Treventis that proves me dead wrong, nobody will be happier than me. I'll need that medication within the next 25 years, if heredity holds true for me.

"They probably won't be any better either."

I look at the mechanism of action, on the rat models and I remain quite bullish on these. But yes, phase II and phase III clinical trials are going to tell the tale.

Here is why it took so long to get to these drugs: We did not understand the mechanism. One dauntless and brave scientist finally pushed his theory forward for a Prion model and that is the underlying cause. So this comes down to refolding/unfolding proteins, something that molecular modeling software is good at predicting with various agents.

Things are really looking up. Be hopeful.

In reference to the news articles I read on Alzheimer's Disease, I feel like Charlie Brown when Lucy pulls the football out again. But I am in good health at this point and I have a lot to be grateful for. The exponential growth of Internet and the growing power of computer hardware and software in medical research gives me the most hope that some sort of treatment that, at the very least, could slow down the rate at which neurodegeneration advances, will be created soon enough to be of benefit to me and others that are younger than me.

You have every reason to be hopeful. Big disease like Alzheimer's have a big payout if they can be cured. Now that the underlying mechanism is revealed, we no longer need to waste time on false associations with things like aluminum, etc.

I give it 10 years for less before we have these therapies reversing AD.
